nodes.label: Flame.frag
nodes.rationale: Fragment shader that evaluates a fully procedural fire field per pixel and discards down to that field's own silhouette; unlit and HDR-bright so bloom does the glow.

nodes.label: Intentionally truncated std140 uniform block
nodes.rationale: std140 offsets are purely positional, so Flame.vert/Flame.frag/Spark.vert declare GlobalUniformBufferObject only up to `time` and omit the trailing lights[] array; nothing before what is read may be skipped or reordered.

nodes.label: Per-pixel procedural fire field
nodes.rationale: The tapered shape, licking structure, translucent fringe and detaching wisps all come from a noise-driven field evaluated per pixel on a flat card, with no fire texture at all.

nodes.label: Unlit emissive shading for fire
nodes.rationale: Fire emits rather than reflects, so there is no lit side or shadow side to compute; the same reasoning is restated for sparks.

nodes.label: Cheap 2D value noise (hash21 + smoothstep)
nodes.rationale: Four hashed cell corners blended with a smoothstep gives grid-free noise with no texture lookups, which is the primitive every other flame field is built from.

nodes.label: 4-octave fBm with 2.02 lacunarity
nodes.rationale: Each octave doubles frequency and halves amplitude for coarse tongues plus fine licking edges; the non-integer 2.02 stops octaves landing on the same grid and showing a repeating overlay.

nodes.label: Wandering flame spine (centreline sway)
nodes.rationale: The sample x is shifted by slow advected noise, zero at the wick and strongest at the tip (y*y), so silhouette and internal structure curl together; called the single biggest difference between pulsing in place and burning.

nodes.label: Power-curve flame width profile
nodes.rationale: pow(1-y, 0.65) instead of a linear or smoothstep taper makes the sides bow outward low down and draw to a point at the top; a linear taper reads as a diamond or kite.

nodes.label: Upward advection of the noise field
nodes.rationale: Subtracting (not adding) time from the sample's y makes the pattern travel up the card -- fuel visibly rising -- and per-layer speed/phase stops the three cards syncing into one pulsing sheet.

nodes.label: Domain warping with a second fBm
nodes.rationale: Offsetting the fBm lookup by a second lower-frequency fBm makes bright regions curl and travel sideways as they rise; with a lateral time term so tongues morph, and warp bite growing with height (laminar at the wick, turbulent at the tip).

nodes.label: Height-dependent noise carving of the silhouette
nodes.rationale: carve = mix(0.35,1.30,y) lets noise barely perturb the dense wick but tear pieces off entirely near the tip, which is how wisps detach; centred on 0.55 because a 4-octave fBm sum sits above the midpoint.

nodes.label: Bubbling hot-gas pockets
nodes.rationale: A thresholded low-frequency field (smoothstep 0.58..0.80) produces distinct blobs with gaps, scrolling ~35% faster than the body so they overtake the texture and read as buoyant volumes; shares the warp so they curl with the surrounding turbulence.

nodes.label: Genuinely translucent outer fringe
nodes.rationale: The alpha window starts well above 0 (smoothstep 0.15..0.50) so the fringe is a real several-pixel gradient rather than saturating to opaque almost immediately.

nodes.label: Alpha discard forced by hardcoded depth writes
nodes.rationale: Starter.hpp hardcodes depthWriteEnable = VK_TRUE on every pipeline including transparent ones, so an undiscarded low-alpha fringe would punch a silhouette-shaped hole through the other flame layers and sparks; discarding is required for correctness, not an optimization.

nodes.label: Four-stop temperature ramp keyed on heat
nodes.rationale: cCold -> cOrange -> cYellow -> cCore is keyed on the noise-carved heat field rather than mesh height, so the whitest pixels sit wherever the noise says the core currently is and drift upward with it.

nodes.label: Hue-rotation recolor of the fire palette
nodes.rationale: Every gradient stop is hue-rotated onto the torch's target color by one shared delta from REF_ORANGE, preserving the dark-to-hot-white value/saturation progression and reproducing the default palette exactly when hueDelta is 0.

nodes.label: custom/FlameColor.glsl (rgb2hsv / hsv2rgb / recolorStop)
nodes.rationale: Shared include holding the HSV conversion and stop-recoloring helpers, so the flame body and its sparks recolor onto `color` in exactly the same way.

nodes.label: HDR boost so bloom has energy to find
nodes.rationale: The hot end is pushed to ~6x while the fringe stays near unit brightness, so bloom flares on the core without the fringe blowing out to white and losing its red/orange.

nodes.label: Per-pixel shimmer varying along the flame
nodes.rationale: A fast noise flicker sampled on (height, time) makes different heights twitch at different moments, reading as combustion; the CPU envelope carries only the slower breathing because the point light must ride that same signal and can't flicker per pixel.

nodes.label: Stare-at glare boost
nodes.rationale: glareBoost is 1.0 unless the player is looking dead-on at the torch, in which case it overdrives the HDR output so bloom flares exactly when the player stares into the flame.
